data.cultural_impact: Garuda is a significant figure in Hindu mythology and is deeply ingrained in both the religious and secular aspects of Indian culture. He is frequently depicted in various forms of art, literature, and folklore. The legendary bird is associated with speed, courage, and valor, making him a popular subject for numerous tales, poetry, and sculpture.
data.spiritual_significance: Garuda is considered to be a divine and auspicious being in Hinduism. He is not only a vehicle for Lord Vishnu but also serves as a protector and a source of spiritual support. In Vedic texts, Garuda is written about as possessing incredible powers and serving as a powerful reminder of the triumph of good over evil. Devotional hymns, prayers, and invocations to Garuda are common in Hindu rituals, both to seek blessings and to receive strength during times of spiritual quests.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Garud from Chennai, India embodies the meaning of Garud - "Eagle". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Garuda is the celestial bird and the vehicle of Lord Vishnu. It signifies freedom and power, with wings spread wide, soaring above earthly constraints. The name embodies courage and vigilance, as Garuda protects dharma and vanquishes evil.

This divine being is considered the vehicle of the god Vishnu and is revered for his strength, agility, and protection. Garud is also believed to be a symbol of freedom and liberation, making it an appealing name for those seeking spiritual growth and enlightenment.
